target_customer: Commercial insurance brokers placing complex, high value risks such as oil rigs
problem: Structuring complicated multi-party commercial insurance deals is slow and done by email and paper; contracts are hard to collaborate on.
business_model: B2B software for brokers to build deals online, pricing not found

founders.name: Dan Hughes
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder with no background.

competitors.name: B3i
competitors.what: Insurer and reinsurer blockchain consortium building shared contract tooling
competitors.traction_then: Revealed a Codex 1 prototype in August 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Deal rooms and enforceable contracts on a blockchain were new in 2017 and legally untested, though a two person team likely built only a thin product.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of customers or integrations; a deal collaboration tool was copyable and large consortia were building similar tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Consortia of insurers were building shared blockchain tools in 2017; Surematics was marked acquired by YC but the acquirer and date were not found.

market_need_then: Complex commercial placements involve many counterparties and long chains, which B3i described as too long; no spend or customer evidence for Surematics was found.

branding.domain_note: surematics.com now redirects to a for-sale domain parking page, so the site is dead.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, no surviving site, and the name (sure plus mathematics) is easily confused with other Sure and Surely insurtechs; the compound reading is my own and not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Surematics was a two person Summer 2017 company aiming to move complex commercial insurance placement online with a blockchain angle. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or terms were found and the site is dead. With no funding, traction or post-mortem found, the cause of the outcome is not public and the record carries no factors.
notes: CB Insights lists about 120K USD seed with YC as investor and shows the company as alive in London; single aggregator, conflicts with YC status, so not recorded as a round. Funding search found no other source. Website surematics.com redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page (not followed). The Round Funded page is a reconstructed application and was not used. Name origin of 'compound' is a type judgment only.
